### Observed differences

- In the later window, six activities became near-universal: A33, A35 and A36 each ran in about 49 of 100 cases before and about 98–99 of 100 after, while A37, A38 and A39 rose from about 51–52 of 100 to about 99 of 100; each runs about once per case where present. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]

- The two groups were mutually exclusive before and are executed together in the later window: previously A33/A35/A36 always ran together (co-occurrence about 48–49 of 100, matching their participation) but essentially never with A37/A38/A39 (cross-group co-occurrence about 1 in 100 or less); in the later window every cross-group pair runs together in about 98 of 100 cases, with the A33/A35/A36 activity coming first in about 95–97 of 100 joint occurrences, while the order within each group stays mixed (both orders in roughly equal shares). [REL037, REL039, REL040, REL041, REL044, REL045, REL046, REL047, REL050, REL051, REL052, REL055, REL059]

- Activities that occur in every case in both windows now bracket the combined block: co-occurrence of A14, A15, A30, A31, A47 and A48 with the block activities rose from about half of cases to about 99 of 100, with A14 and A30 preceding the block (about 95–98 of 100), A31 and A47/A48 following it, and A15 partly interleaved (about 41 of 100). [REL013, REL014, REL018, REL019, REL025, REL026, REL030, REL031, REL033, REL036, REL042, REL048, REL053, REL057, REL060, REL062]

- Routing around the block was rewired: A30's outgoing transitions, previously spread over both groups (A35, A36, A37, A38, A39 each about 14–18%), now concentrate on A35, A33 and A36 (about 29–36% each) with A37/A38/A39 near zero; A33, A35 and A36 now lead on to A37, A38 and A39 (about 7–13% each) and no longer directly to A31 (from about 27–34% of their outgoing transitions to under 1%). [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]

- Position gaps grew where the block grew: distances from A30 to A37/A38/A39 and from A33/A35/A36 to A31 moved from mostly 1–3 positions to mostly 4–5 positions, consistent with the other group now running in between. [LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG011, LAG013]

- A04 receded: it ran in about 59 of 100 cases before and about 26 of 100 after; the share of A04's outgoing transitions going to A15 fell from about 90% to about 40%; A04 now sits later in the case (mean relative position about 0.20 vs 0.38), and in the later window about 74 of 100 cases contain a block activity but not A04. [OCC002, DIR002, DIR004, POS001, REL005, REL008, REL010]

- Rare activities rose and minor shifts appeared: A02 about 6 → 18, A08 about 7.5 → 18 and A10 about 5.5 → 22 of 100 cases, showing up as small new successors of A14, A45 and A47 (profiles based on only about 11–50 outgoing transitions per window); A30 sits slightly earlier and A31 slightly later, and the immediate A47→A48 succession fell from about 96 to about 84 of 100 cases. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, DIR009, DIR010, POS003, POS004, LAG015]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the exclusive choice between two alternative activity groups was removed: before, each case executed either the group A33/A35/A36 (about 49 in 100 cases) or the group A37/A38/A39 (about 51 in 100), never both, whereas in the later window all six activities execute in about 98–99 of 100 cases, with the first group preceding the second in about 95–97 of 100 joint occurrences and the order within each group remaining unfixed. This alternatives-to-joint-execution change is shown directly for every cross-group pair, is consistent across the participation, relation, direction and distance indicators, and the screening context makes chance an implausible explanation of the pattern as a whole (109 qualifying control-flow items against about 1 expected without change). [REL039, REL041, REL045, REL047, REL050, REL052, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, LAG005, LAG008]

Limitations: the evidence cannot show whether the combined block is now strictly mandatory, since about 1–2 of 100 later cases still miss individual block activities, and it cannot distinguish a routing change from a shift in the mix of case types entering the process; the occurrence, position and relation items for the same activities describe the same traces, so they corroborate rather than independently confirm the change. [OCC005, OCC008, REL039, REL050]

Other differences: A04's decline — participation about 59 → 26 of 100 cases, its dominant link to A15 falling from about 90% to about 40% of its outgoing transitions, and a later position in the case — is a separate participation change not covered by the block hypothesis; the rises of A02, A08 and A10 also stand apart but rest on few observations. [OCC002, DIR002, DIR004, POS001, OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, DIR009, DIR010]

Now, what do the items say?

OCC items:

- OCC002: A04 participation 0.59 → 0.255 (59% → ~26%), mean 0.635 → 0.315. Support 118 → 51.
- OCC003: A08 participation 0.075 → 0.18 (7.5% → 18%). Support 15 → 36.

- OCC005: A33 participation 0.49 → 0.985 (49% → ~99%). Support 98 → 197.

- OCC007: A36 participation 0.49 → 0.985. Support 98 → 197.

So a block of activities A33, A35, A36, A37, A38, A39 went from being in about half the traces to nearly all traces. A02, A08, A10 roughly tripled/quadrupled from rare (~5-7%) to ~18-22%. A04 dropped from ~59% to ~26%.
